1                                             STIPULATION

2           This stipulation is entered into by and between Plaintiff Gen Digital Inc. (f/k/a Symantec

3    Corporation) (“Gen”) and Defendant Sycomp, A Technology Company, Inc. (“Sycomp”)

4    (collectively, the “Parties”), by and through their respective attorneys of record, pursuant to

5    Northern District Local Rule 7-11 and/or Norther District Local Rule 6-2.

6           WHEREAS, on July 8, 2024, Gen filed a Complaint (the “Complaint”) in this action

7    (Dkt. 1) against Sycomp and North American Systems International, Inc. (“NASI”) (collectively,

8    “Defendants”) for breach of contract;

9           WHEREAS, on October 31, 2024, following Defendants’ successful motions to dismiss,

10   Gen filed a First Amended Complaint (“FAC”) against Sycomp and NASI (Dkt. 42);

11          WHEREAS, on November 14, 2024, Sycomp filed a motion to dismiss the Second and

12   Fifth Claims for Relief of the FAC (Dkt. 44);

13          WHEREAS, on November 14, 2024, Sycomp filed a partial motion to dismiss all but the

14   First Claim for Relief in the FAC (Dkt. 44);

15          WHEREAS, on November 14, 2024, NASI filed a motion to dismiss all claims against it

16   in the FAC (Dkt. 48);

17          WHEREAS, on January 6, 2025, the Court granted Defendants’ motions to dismiss,

18   dismissing all of the claims against NASI without leave to amend and all but the First Claim for

19   Relief against Sycomp (“Dismissal Order”) (Dkt. 55);

20          WHEREAS, on February 27, 2025, Sycomp filed a motion for judgment on the pleadings

21   as to the remaining First Claim for Relief (Dkt. 59);

22          WHEREAS, on March 11, 2025, NASI filed a notice of motion and motion for entry of

23   final judgment pursuant to Rule 54(b) (Dkt. 66);

24          WHEREAS, on March 24, 2025, the Court denied Sycomp’s motion for judgment on the

25   pleadings (Dkt. 70) (“Order Denying Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings”);

26   //

27   //

28

1           WHEREAS, on March 25, 2025, Gen filed a notice of non-opposition to NASI’s motion

2    for entry of final judgment (Dkt. 71), and on March 26, 2025, the Court granted NASI’s motion

3    (Dkt. 72) and entered judgment in favor of NASI (“NASI Judgment”) (Dkt. 73);

4           WHEREAS, on April 25, 2025, Gen filed a notice of appeal of the Dismissal Order and

5    the NASI Judgment (Dkt. 78);

6           WHEREAS, on April 30, 2025, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit filed a

7    Docketing Notice and Time Schedule Order (Dkt. No. 79);

8           WHEREAS, on July 10, 2025, Gen filed Appellant’s Opening Brief and thus an appeal of

9    this Court’s Orders granting NASI’s motion to dismiss and dismissing NASI from this action

10   was pending at that time;
11          WHEREAS, on August 1, 2025, the parties stipulated to a stay of all proceedings in this
12   matter until further order of the Court pending resolution of Plaintiff’s appeal of the Court’s
13   judgment in favor of NASI, citing Landis v. North American Co., 299 U.S. 248, 254 (1936), and,
14   pursuant to the Parties’ stipulation, this Court entered an order staying all proceedings in this
15   action (Dkt. 84) (“Stay Order”);
16          WHEREAS, on December 30, 2025, the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth
17   Circuit issued a memorandum affirming this Court’s Rule 54(b) Judgment in favor of NASI
18   (“Decision”) and, on January 21, 2026, issued an Order Denying Petition for Panel Rehearing
19   (“Rehearing Order”);
20          WHEREAS, under a court’s inherent powers described in Landis, a court may lift a stay

21   that it had entered based on economy of time and effort for itself, counsel, and the litigants when

22   the circumstances motivating the stay no longer exist;

23          WHEREAS, on January 29, 2026, Gen filed a Notice of Decision and Rehearing Order

24   pursuant to the Stay Order (Dkt. 85), and the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth

25   Circuit issued a Mandate on the Appeal (Dkt. 86, Exs. A-C), thereby deciding the appeal and

26   removing the circumstances motivating the stay;

27          WHEREAS, Sycomp’s motion for judgment on the pleadings argued that “the Solaris

28

1    Patches” at issue in this case “were not provided under or covered by the” Parties’ Product

2    Purchase Agreement (“PPA”) because “Plaintiff does not allege the existence of any mutually

3    executed Order Instrument related to the Solaris Patches” (Dkt. 59 at 1);

4           WHEREAS, in its Order Denying Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings, the Court

5    noted: “If discovery reveals that there was no mutually executed purchase order for Solaris

6    patches, a targeted early motion for summary judgment may be appropriate.” (Dkt. 70 at 3-4 & n

7    1);

8           WHEREAS, in its case management discretion, the Court may order phased proceedings,

9    such as a targeted early motion for summary judgment to simplify issues and facilitate the just,

10   speedy, and inexpensive disposition of the action; see Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(c)(2)(A), (c)(2)(P);
11          WHEREAS, although due process requires that Gen receive the opportunity to adduce
12   facts to justify an opposition to a targeted motion for summary judgment, there has been little
13   discovery to this point in the action, and thus the Parties are agreeable to a proposed schedule
14   that gives the parties the time to conduct limited additional discovery into the “Order Instrument”
15   issues prior to such a targeted early summary judgment motion under Rule 56(d)(2);
16          WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 1.C of General Standing Order for Civil and Criminal
17   Cases Before Judge Charles R. Breyer, the parties agree that there is good cause to exceed the
18   limitation of one summary judgment motion per party to allow a targeted summary judgment
19   motion on the Order Instrument factual and legal issues, including the existence or non-existence
20   of mutually executed purchase orders and the appropriate construction of the relevant provision

21   of the PPA concerning “Order Instruments” relating to Solaris patches and the necessity or lack

22   of necessity for mutual execution of purchase orders;

23

24          IT IS HEREBY STIPULATED by and between the Parties, through their respective

25   Counsel, that the stay of this action as set forth in the Stay Order should be lifted;

26          IT IS HEREBY FURTHER STIPULATED THAT targeted early summary judgment

27   proceedings on the Order Instruments factual and legal issues are appropriate to determine if the

28

2    the Parties consent to such proceedings;

3             IT IS HEREBY FURTHER STIPULATED THAT the Parties are agreeable to

4    undertaking additional discovery limited to the Order Instrument issues under Rule 56(d)(2),

5    including discovery related to interpretation of the PPA, but that all other discovery shall remain

6    stayed until further ordered by the Court;

7             ACCORDINGLY, IT IS HEREBY FURTHER STIPULATED THAT the Parties propose

8    the following case management, discovery and pre-trial schedule—through the hearing of the

1                                          [PROPOSED] ORDER

2           GOOD CAUSE APPEARING THEREFOR, and in accordance with the above Stipulation

3    IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT:

4           1.       The stay in this matter issued August 8, 2025 is lifted;

5           2.       The proposed discovery, motion and pre-trial schedule set forth above is hereby

6    approved; and

7           3.       To resolve factual and legal issues regarding “Order Instruments” within the

8    meaning of the Parties’ Product Purchase Agreement:

9                    a.     The Parties shall undertake discovery on such “Order Instrument” issues

10          pursuant to the approved discovery, motion and pre-trial schedule; and

11                   b.     Defendant shall file a targeted motion for summary judgment on the “Order

12          Instrument” issues and Plaintiff shall oppose it pursuant to the briefing schedule within the

13          approved discovery, motion and pre-trial schedule.

14
